profiles.field_rule: Research trial: a small annual with a densely contracted or somewhat interrupted, spike-like panicle, a true short membranous ligule and very short (0–3 mm) lemma awns. Do not use a broken or unexamined floret to choose 'no obvious long awns'; skip that character if damaged. Verify lower 1-veined and upper 3-veined glumes, fertile floret count and actual awn origin before calling the species. Compare other compact pooid grasses.

profiles.field_rule: Research trial: look for a thin cylindrical jointed raceme, with spikelets fitting closely into recesses in the axis. Check the sessile fertile and stalked sterile pair and pitted glume on the same specimen. The source name Coelorachis cylindrica refers to this profile. A small cluster may have short knotty rhizomes; inspect the tiny membrane and its ragged hair-edged rim inside the collar. Awn state remains unknown here, not scored as absent. Compare jointed goatgrass and other jointed grasses by actual spikelet arrangement.
